text:
Tye Kartye went undrafted, scored his way out of the AHL in Seattle's system, and spent last season as a 12-minute depth forward. This season the Rangers have handed him almost 17 minutes a night, a spot on the power play he never had, and he's answered with seven goals and 14 points in 24 games, plus a heavy physical game (61 hits). Local coverage has started talking about locking him up before his price climbs.

This breakout looks real to us. His own chances have more than doubled, to about one expected goal per 60 minutes from under half that, and his seven goals match his 6.8 expected almost exactly. No hot shooting here. At five on five New York gets 57% of the expected goals with him on the ice, six points better than without him.

If anything, he's been unlucky. The Rangers have scored seven fewer goals than their chances deserve with Kartye out there, which has cost him points, and that usually swings back. His recent ice time is up near 19 minutes. Watch whether he keeps it as the lineup gets healthier.
headline: Kartye's bigger role is built on real chances
